items.meaning: Feed-mode assignment matches on the documented Fanuc-style and Haas lathes.
items.notes: Both use G98 for feed per minute and G99 for feed per revolution in the lathe context documented here. The meanings differ on mills, and control options can vary, so verify the exact machine manual before transferring code.

items.meaning: Inch and metric input work the same on both, but Haas users must confirm Setting 9.
items.notes: Both brands use G20 for inch input and G21 for metric input. On Haas controls, G20 and G21 check Setting 9 (Inch/Metric) rather than converting stored coordinates. Other controls may differ, so verify the active unit mode.

On Fanuc-style lathes G50 commonly clamps maximum spindle RPM (used with G96 constant surface speed). On some other controls G50 sets the coordinate system. Never assume — verify the machine manual before using G50.

items.meaning: Canned-cycle parameter formats vary by control generation.
items.notes: The letter order and the use of a one-line or two-line format differ among Fanuc generations and other brands, including Haas. A control may misread a cycle block copied verbatim from another brand. Match the exact format in your control's programming manual.

items.meaning: Gear-range and chuck codes are builder-defined rather than universal.
items.notes: M41 and M42 for gear ranges and M23 and M24 for chuck control exist on some machines, but they are not standard Fanuc codes. The machine builder assigns them. For example, they may appear on a Johnford HT 60CX-2D. Do not assume that these codes will work; check the builder's manual. M00 through M30 are the nearly universal set.

items.meaning: Verify each code against your machine's manual rather than relying on a generic list.
items.notes: Fanuc publishes manuals for individual models, such as the 0i-T and 18i-T, while Haas publishes model-specific code pages. Builder options, parameter settings, and ladder logic can remap codes. These lists are learning aids. The machine manual and a dry run or single-block prove-out are the final authorities.
